- Overestimate prices in the short term after sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment > 0.33) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is neutral or negative — model fails to recognize mean reversion or risk-off behavior.
- Forecast bias toward higher prices in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is flat (all 0.00) — model overconfident in upward momentum.
- Lag in price correction after spikes — model delays recognizing true turning points, especially after sentiment drops.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves — model reacts too aggressively, peaking too early and then falling sharply.
- Mean reversion bias — model holds onto upward momentum longer than actual price behavior, especially in 30-day horizon.
- Sentiment history with 0.00 values should trigger conservative adjustments — avoid overbought forecasts.
- When sentiment is > 0.33, model should reduce forecast volatility — avoid overfitting to recent spikes.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating late-period corrections — adjust downward for final 5–7 days if sentiment is flat.
